title: Visit to Boston made Boca Raton resident feel miserable about living in Boca Raton
author: Elizabeth Mehler
bullets: Ian Pinto's trip to Boston highlighted stark differences with his hometown Boca Raton, inspiring a Reddit post.
Pinto appreciated Boston's walkability, public transportation, and cost of living compared to Boca Raton.
Pinto praised Boston's inclusive community and expressed a desire to eventually move there.

title: Motorcyclist killed in crash with pickup truck in Raynham
author: Elizabeth Mehler
bullets: A 31-year-old motorcyclist, Jason Marshall, was killed in a collision with a pickup truck in Raynham.
The crash occurred around 8 p.m. at the intersection of Route 138 and Elm Street.
The 2015 Chevy Silverado driver, a 57-year-old man, stayed at the scene and cooperated with police.

title: N.H. police seek to identify suspects who fatally shot dog in attempted armed robbery
author: Elizabeth Mehler
bullets: A dog was fatally shot during an attempted armed robbery in Hollis, New Hampshire, early Tuesday morning.
The victim had arranged to meet a woman online, but encountered two armed suspects demanding money.
Police seek residents' security footage from 2 a.m. to 4 a.m. Tuesday to identify the fleeing suspects.

title: Former Red Sox infielder criticized front office: ‘Some people watch the game, some people go on the computer’
author: Hayden Bird
bullets: Former Red Sox infielder Vaughn Grissom criticized the team's analytics-heavy approach, attributing his underperformance there to lack of belief.
Grissom, traded to the Angels, now plays regularly and attributes his success to organizational trust rather than changes in his play.
Grissom acknowledged no hard feelings towards Boston teammates but wished for more opportunities to prove himself in the lineup.

title: Authorities investigating 4 family members shot in N.H. as potential attempted murders and suicide
author: Elizabeth Mehler
bullets: A potential attempted murder-suicide left four family members shot in Whitefield, N.H., involving multiple gunshot injuries.
Eric Blake Jr., 29, died from a self-inflicted gunshot; three others, including Amy Blake, remain hospitalized.
Eric Blake Sr. drove to a hospital after being shot and is in stable condition; investigation is ongoing.

title: Livestream: Lindsay Clancy murder trial continues with her psychiatric treatment in the spotlight
author: Abby Patkin
bullets: The murder trial of Lindsay Clancy focuses on her psychiatric treatment and the involvement of mental health professionals.
Massachusetts State Police Sgt. Daniel Lawlor testified about a psychologist's alleged influence on Clancy during hospitalization.
Prosecutors allege Clancy deliberately killed her children, while the defense cites postpartum mental illness and insanity.

title: Acton teen located after police discover two dead in home
author: Ross Cristantiello
bullets: Police located 17-year-old Arjun Aravind after two deaths in an Acton home on Martha Lane.
A woman and teenage boy were found dead; the cause and manner of death remain under investigation.
Aravind was initially missing with a 2014 green Honda Accord, which was later found in Wayland.

title: Q&A: Boston’s nightlife czar says the city is just getting started
author: Beth Treffeisen
bullets: Boston's nightlife is evolving with extended bar hours and the establishment of social districts for outdoor drinking.
Boston's nightlife economy director, Corean Reynolds, reports increased revenue and enthusiasm from local businesses.
Future plans include less restrictive alcohol laws and improved late-night transportation to support the nightlife economy.

title: Recent homes sales in Greater Boston (Aug. 12)
author: The Boston Globe
bullets: A Boston condo at 46 Beacon St. sold for $18 million, the highest sale in the report.
An Acton Colonial at 5 Westside Drive sold for $925,000, featuring 1,926 square feet and three bedrooms.
A Bedford Colonial on Goldman Circle sold for $2.825 million, offering 4,510 square feet and five bedrooms.

title: Nearly 50 children recovered during anti-human trafficking operation in Greater Boston during the World Cup, officials say
author: Samantha Genzer
bullets: 48 missing and endangered children were recovered during the World Cup in a Greater Boston anti-trafficking operation.
Operation Yellow Card involved collaboration among U.S. Marshals, Massachusetts State Police, and Boston Police Department.
The initiative targeted human trafficking and led to further investigations into child exploitation and related crimes.
